A.question: Are 100 contiguous official US House rollcalls equivalent to 100 distinct underlying agenda issues for naive PFL scoring opportunity measurement?
A.unit: 2025 U.S. House Clerk rollcall numbers 200 through 299 (inclusive) × textual official Issue label
A.population: This contiguous roll-number segment, not a random national/year sample
outcomes: share of rollcalls whose official Issue label repeats in the same segment
A.estimand: 100 rollcalls vs number of distinct legislative issues, no moral or personal score
A.interference: rollcalls on same bill are mechanically dependent

B.h1: More than 15% of rollcalls share an Issue label with at least one other rollcall
B.h2: Multiple votes on one bill are different substantive decisions so issue-capping discards legitimate events
B.h0: little issue repetition in this segment

C.source: Official Office of Clerk House roll call index 2025 from roll calls 200–299 link
C.QA: full contiguous numbers and dates, no missing, issues named uniformly; no inferred first-public timestamps; cite first-party page
analysis: group exact Issue strings, classify missing Issue separately
comparators: one-point-per-distinct-exact-issue only as sensitivity, not a normative score
C.novelty: Known legislative procedure; exploratory instrument diagnostic, not original causal finding

D.rights: Official House Clerk information, no person-level votes, no political profiles
D.instrumentation: retrieve webpage and transcribe issue labels with full rollcall 200–299 QA; if unable to obtain all, STOP_LOCAL / NOT_EXECUTED
